newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Ofwat warns water firms on div payouts.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Ofwat warns water firms on div payouts.

text.p: Britain's water industry watchdog Ofwat warned companies on Tuesday not to undermine investment by paying out hefty dividend increases.

"I am...concerned that companies should fulfill their investment programmes and that unjustifiably high dividend increases do not undermine that," Ofwat head Ian Byatt said in a statement announcing publication of the annual report.
Byatt said he considered that sharing savings from changes in capital programmes had worked well.
He reiterated his view that customers should not end up paying for a one-off tax on the excess profits of privatised utilities planned by the new Labour government.
"I have said that I believe customers want the tax to be paid by shareholders, not by them," Byatt said.

Thames Water Plc, the company which supplies the country's capital London, said on Tuesday that investments could be hit if the "windfall" tax were too severe as it reported a 19 percent rise in year pretax profits to 384 million stg and raised its dividend 22 percent.
Byatt said companies needed "to understand better the balance between available water, consumption and leakage."
He said he expected the amount of water lost through leaks to come down by at least 15 percent from 1995-96 figures.
The government has set up a 10-point plan aimed at coping with the country's current drought, which includes mandatory leakage limit targets.

Byatt said he was disappointed that only a few companies had made progress in developing a methodology to calculate the "economic" level of leakage at which costs of repairs do not outweigh supply savings benefits.
